title: Atlas Cold Chain
tagline: Sensor-native refrigeration for last-mile biologics in Sun Belt metros.

sections.body: Atlas installs retrofit IoT cold pods inside independent pharmacy networks, synchronizing temperature proofs with insurer-grade audit trails. We sell compliance as a subscription, not hardware capex.

Biologic prescriptions grew 4.1× in southern states over five years, while carrier reliability flatlined. Regulatory scrutiny on spoilage is tightening; pharmacies need passive telemetry, not clipboard logs.
Edge firmware on Nordic silicon, redundant probes, and a web dashboard that lawyers actually enjoy reading. Patent pending on our thermal fingerprinting heuristic.
Piloted with 38 locations across Austin and Phoenix. 99.992% uptime on readings, −41% insurance rider premiums in early cohort, $190k ARR under LOIs.
Expand field engineering pod, certify two additional states, and ship API hooks for Epic-sidecar integrations. Marketing stays founder-led until Series A narrative is airtight.
$320k hires (2 firmware, 1 compliance), $210k inventory float, $190k regulatory counsel & certifications, $130k working capital buffer.
Q3: 120 live pods. Q4: SOC 2 Type I complete. Q1 next year: channel partnership with top-three regional wholesaler.

Hardware lead times, state-by-state pharmacy board quirks, potential copycats from legacy cold-chain giants. Mitigation: modular BOM, aggressive documentation, and exclusivity windows with anchor tenants.
Seeking $850k on a SAFE plus side letter outlining 9% equity at next priced round, with pro-rata for strategic operators who open doors in healthcare distribution.

title: Lumen Notebooks
tagline: Local-first notebooks where every cell knows your team's semantic graph.

sections.body: Lumen fuses collaborative notebooks with on-device embeddings so analysts can query institutional memory without shipping raw data to the cloud. Think 'Figma meets Wolfram' for quant and policy teams.
Fortune 500 analytics units are paralyzed between ChatGPT curiosity and infosec terror. Buyers want LLM ergonomics with deterministic audit logs—budget lines now exist, not just pilots.
Rust core, CRDT sync, optional air-gapped mode. Model adapters plug in like VS Code extensions. Every export is a signed Merkle tree for compliance officers who lose sleep.
Design partners in fintech and defense; 620 weekly active devs on private beta; waitlist north of 4k. Paid POC averaging $27k ARR equivalent.
Ship enterprise SSO, finalize SOC 2, hire developer relations lead from a household-name IDE, and run a controlled launch in regulated industries first—glamour later.
$480k engineering, $260k security audits, $220k GTM experiments, $240k reserve for GPU appliance bundles for offline clients.
90 days: SOC 2 Type I underway. 180 days: three referenceable enterprise logos. 270 days: marketplace for third-party model adapters.

Incumbent notebook vendors could clone features; hiring security talent is expensive; model licensing is a maze. Mitigation: OSS wedge, advisory board with former regulators, ruthless focus on auditability.
Raising $1.2M seed extension at 11% equity for a partner who understands developer tooling GTM and can navigate procurement in regulated stacks.

title: Harbor Compost Collective
tagline: Neighborhood-scale compost that pays apartment towers for their organics stream.

sections.body: Harbor places modular digesters in multifamily parking structures, turning food waste into certified soil amendments sold to regional growers. Revenue shares flow back to buildings as ESG storytelling fuel.

Coastal cities are passing organics mandates faster than haulers can adapt. Property managers need turnkey compliance without smell complaints—we deliver odor-neutral industrial design and SMS alerts.
Carbon-fiber reinforced vessels, biofilter stack, and a logistics OS that syncs with existing waste brokers. Smells like nothing; dashboards smell like victory.
Two towers live in San Diego, diverting 38 tons monthly. LOIs for six additional assets. Soil offtake agreements at 112% of model price.
Fabricate fourth-generation vessel with faster clean-out, onboard a municipal advisor, and lock rolling fund vehicle for asset co-investors.
$160k manufacturing deposit, $95k permitting sprint, $85k sales engineer, $70k working capital for soil blending partnerships.
6 months: five towers. 12 months: franchisable playbook for Sunbelt cities. 18 months: offtake contracts covering 80% of output.
Zoning delays, commodity swings in compost pricing, equipment wear in salty air. Mitigation: legal templates per city, hedged offtake, marine-grade coatings.
Seeking $410k for 7% equity plus board observer rights for a partner with climate fund credibility and multifamily operator relationships.
